comments.story: James Lovelock has died
comments.text: Despite everything else he accomplished in his quite storied professional career as one of the last independent scientists... Including his work on the Viking mars landers! [LINK] To me he will always be the man who invented his own microwave to thaw frozen hamsters. The whole story is worth a watch since Tom Scott does an admirable job of explaining how he went digging up a weird fact expecting to debunk it only to wind up recording an amazing interview with James Lovelock [VIDEO] but if you’re impatient the interview with lovelock about cryopreserved hamsters and his "microwave" starts here [VIDEO]

comments.story: Scientists unfroze rat organs and transplanted them
comments.text: Tom Scott made a great video about it, he even got to the guy who started using microwaves for thawing entire small animals. Before microwaves (diathermic heating) they would use a hot piece of metal, like a large spoon. [VIDEO] And yes, you can unfreeze a rock solid rat, then see it walk around. This is why cryogenics was hyped so much, because it sort of works on small animals.

comments.story: A singular scientist: James Lovelock
comments.text: Tom Scott interviewed him last year in a really wonderful video about microwaves.
